findings.trigger: Every passing run writes the hardcoded value 'Python3.10.22 pinned first image'.
findings.impact: The evidence names an end-of-life runtime as the canonical candidate. The stated candidate is 3.13.15. Token counts already differ: the unicode fixture gives 20 on 3.10 and 19 on 3.12/3.13. Any token guard derived from this record would be calibrated to the wrong runtime.
findings.remediation: Derive the candidate from the 3.13 entry by image digest and observed sys.version. Record the token counts for that runtime as canonical.

findings.trigger: The timeout and kill canary always runs on the 3.10 image.
findings.impact: The kill and removal path is never observed on the pinned 3.13 image.
findings.remediation: Run the timeout canary on the 3.13 digest, or on all three images.

findings.trigger: call raises TimeoutExpired or RuntimeError after the daemon has already created or started the container.
findings.impact: The name is never added to owned, so the finally block skips it. The container can leak, and allOwnedContainersAbsent can still report true because it only checks tracked names.
findings.remediation: Append the name to owned before create/run. Cleanup already tolerates absent containers via check=False.

findings.locator: call('kill',name); assert call('inspect',name,check=False).returncode!=0; and the final allOwnedContainersAbsent check
findings.trigger: Removal under --rm is asynchronous, so inspect can run before the daemon finishes removing the container.
findings.impact: This can cause flaky false failures, or leave a stale running container reported as present. It does not cause a false pass.
findings.remediation: Use a bounded 'wait' with removal confirmation (e.g. poll inspect within a fixed deadline) before asserting absence.

findings.locator: memory canary and root-write canary in code
findings.trigger: The memoryCanaryDenied check relies only on a self-set RLIMIT_AS. The write canary accepts EACCES, which a nonroot user receives on '/' even when the root filesystem is writable.
findings.impact: The in-container canaries do not demonstrate cgroup memory enforcement or a read-only rootfs. Only the host-side inspect assertions back those claims. The /tmp size and noexec settings are never observed.
findings.remediation: Label the memory canary as rlimit-only. Require EROFS for the root-write canary. Add read checks of /proc/mounts for /tmp (noexec, size) and the rootfs read-only flag.

coverage: Docker env and config isolation: allowlisted variables, empty DOCKER_CONFIG, fixed engine pipe.
Container flags verified via inspect: network none, read-only rootfs, uid, memory, pids, no bind mounts, env-name allowlist.
In-container cgroup values, RLIMIT_NPROC spawn denial, network denial, fixed literal fixtures parsed without being executed.
Cross-image declaration digest agreement; three invalid fixtures rejected.
Cleanup paths, timeout canary, and failure-message withholding.
gaps: feature_version=(3,10) on 3.13 is best-effort. Grammar parity with 3.10 is shown only by the single except* fixture.
No CPU-exhaustion or AST-depth canary inside the pinned 3.13 image.
The 5s per-instance and 15s overall deadlines are not implemented or tested here (out of scope by statement).
The evidence file is written to an absolute host path with no integrity binding to the harness source.
